public_rationale: He presents this as his reading ('suggesting, I believe'): OpenAI taking over Microsoft's CoreWeave option is a sign that Microsoft is disconnecting from OpenAI. 'Disconnecting' has no stated measure. Later events point both ways. In October 2025, Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal on new OpenAI cloud work, but OpenAI committed to buy an extra $250 billion of Azure services. The side remark that OpenAI is 'at least on paper' CoreWeave's largest customer is hedged. OpenAI's deal added $11.2 billion of backlog, but the filings as summarized do not show Microsoft's share of the rest. With a hedged reading of motive and no measure, the claim is not graded.
limitations: Under a loose reading, the loss of Microsoft's right of first refusal could count as partial disconnection. Under a strict one, the $250B Azure commitment would count against it.
